skill.name: production-code-audit
skill.description: Guides an AI agent through a production-readiness audit covering security, performance, architecture, testing, documentation, and remediation.
skill.summary: Audit codebases for production readiness across security, performance, architecture, tests, and documentation.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline tool names, resource links, and illustrative before-and-after code. No executable command, network fetch, secret exfiltration, or weak cryptography implementation was found. The main risk is the prose instruction to read and modify the whole repository automatically without user confirmation.

remediation.suggestion: Require the user to confirm the audit scope before reading the full repository. Exclude secrets, generated files, dependencies, and build artifacts by default.
Present a remediation plan and ask for approval before editing files. Apply changes in small batches and report every modified file.

remediation.issue: Markdown examples trigger static security scanners
remediation.suggestion: Label examples as non-executable documentation and avoid fenced snippets that look like active commands when plain text is enough.

static_findings.snippet: const query = \`SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '\${email}'\`;
- Use `listDirectory` to find all files recursively
- Use `readFile` to read every source file
- Use `strReplace` to fix issues in files

semantic_findings.description: The skill tells the agent to read every file recursively and fix everything automatically without user input. This can expose sensitive files and cause unintended repository changes.

content.value_statement: Production releases need review across security, performance, testing, and architecture. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through a structured production audit.
actual_capabilities: Maps project structure, entry points, architecture, and data flow from repository files.
Checks security risks such as SQL injection, hardcoded secrets, weak hashing, and missing validation.
Reviews performance risks including N+1 queries, missing indexes, large bundles, and inefficient algorithms.
Identifies testing, documentation, logging, monitoring, and deployment readiness gaps.
Provides a prioritized audit report template with findings, grades, actions, and timelines.
Instructs the agent to propose fixes, apply approved changes, and verify results with tests.
limitations: The skill is a guidance file, not a standalone static analysis engine.
Results depend on repository access, available tools, and the agent model.
Large repositories may need scoping to avoid slow or noisy analysis.
Security findings still need human review before production deployment.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Service for Launch
use_cases.description: Review architecture, security, tests, performance, and documentation before a production release.

use_cases.title: Harden an Existing Web App
use_cases.description: Find missing validation, weak secret handling, authentication gaps, and dependency risks in a live codebase.

use_cases.title: Create a Remediation Plan
use_cases.description: Turn a broad audit into prioritized actions with owners, risk levels, and estimated timelines.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Production Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this repository for production readiness. Summarize critical issues first, then list safe next steps before editing files.

prompt_templates.title: Security-Focused Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review authentication, input validation, secrets handling, and dependency posture. Propose fixes with file references and test coverage needs.

prompt_templates.title: Full Hardening Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a prioritized production hardening plan for this codebase. Include architecture, performance, observability, testing, and deployment risks with effort estimates.

prompt_templates.title: Approved Fix Pass
prompt_templates.prompt: After producing an audit plan, apply only the approved high-severity fixes. Run relevant tests and report changed files and remaining risks.

output_examples.input: Audit this Express and React app before launch.
output_examples.output: A prioritized report lists missing admin authorization, weak input validation, slow product queries, low test coverage, and deployment checklist gaps.

output_examples.input: Secure this repository and show what needs approval.
output_examples.output: The response separates critical security fixes from advisory items, explains file impact, and asks before applying repository-wide changes.

output_examples.input: Create a production readiness plan for the next sprint.
output_examples.output: The plan groups actions by security, reliability, performance, and testing, with estimated effort and verification steps.

best_practices: Define the repository scope and deployment target before running a full audit.
Review and approve the proposed remediation plan before broad edits.
Run tests, linters, and security scans after each high-impact change.
anti_patterns: Running automatic fixes across a large repository without reviewing the plan.
Treating example security checks as proof that the application is compliant.
Skipping human review for authentication, authorization, and data handling changes.

faq.question: Does this skill change files automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide file changes, but users should require approval before broad edits.

faq.question: Can it replace a professional security audit?
faq.answer: No. It helps find common issues, but production security still needs qualified review.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What kinds of issues does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers security, performance, architecture, testing, documentation, and deployment readiness.

faq.question: Is it useful for small projects?
faq.answer: Yes. Scope the audit to critical paths so the output stays focused.

faq.question: How should teams use the final report?
faq.answer: Review the findings, approve fixes, assign owners, and verify changes with tests.
